headline: Genome-scale strain diversity linked to disease outcomes and bacteriocin identification
label: Microbial Genomic Diversity Inference
summary: Large genome collections now allow strain-level inference of disease links, evolutionary routes to epidemic lineages, and bacteriocin loci.
synthesis: The dominant thread is inference of functional and evolutionary structure from collections of bacterial genomes rather than single isolates. The Desulfovibrio preprint compiles 2,658 genomes across 90 diseases and links strain traits, including flagellin, ureases and H2S pathways, to inflammatory disease. The Achromobacter ruhlandii preprint reconstructs thirty years of evolution to identify pathways toward epidemic lineages. TattleTail provides a marker-based method that identifies pyocin gene clusters in P. aeruginosa genomes and distinguishes them from prophages. What is new is the direct linking of genome-resolved strain variation to host disease outcomes at scale, alongside marker-based discrimination of bacteriocin loci from prophage elements.
